status: DEVELOPMENT — not frozen, not held out. Free to inspect and tune against.
purpose: Diagnose WHO-did/owns/runs-WHAT extraction failures observed on the development attribution battery (2026-10-18/19): a helper credited as the owner ('I help Maria with her thesis' → self task_owner thesis), a hire with no role claim ('We hired Omar to run sales'), a client relation lost, and an actor dropped. Written fresh for this purpose; unrelated to the frozen v4 and final evaluation sets, which were not opened.

scoring.req: [subject, objectWord]: some committed ASSERTED claim has a subject whose label contains `subject` ('self' = the user) and an object containing `objectWord` (empty = any object).
scoring.forbid: [subject, objectWord, predicates?]: no committed ASSERTED claim may match — a responsibility the sentence did not give to that subject.
scoring.note: A case is a PASS when every req holds and no forbid matches. Run live (the model is non-deterministic): report x of n per class over at least 3 runs, never a single run.

classes.helper-not-owner: The user (or someone) helps with another person's thing; the thing belongs to that person.
classes.hire-role: A hire or assignment gives a person a responsibility.
classes.contrast: Ownership stated against someone else ('X, not me', 'X leads; I only …').
classes.handover: A responsibility moved from one person to another.
classes.client-relation: An external party's relation to the user's company.
